text:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: prod kv-cache error rate + token latency spike detected for inference-v2. auto-page to #incidents and oncall-tiers.

incident-bot: Summary: sudden 8x increase in kv cache misses + continuous-batching backlog. Suspected prefix hash collisions after tokenizer rollout.

sara.nguyen: seeing 95th percentile token latency jump from 120ms -> 1.2s on region-us-east1. A bunch of 504s from customer webhooks.

mike.roy: confirmed. Grafana shows a sharp increase in kv-store ops and mem pressure on batch-workers. Paging @oncall_tier2.

oncall_tier2: on it. pulling timeline now. any recent changes to tokenizer / prefix hashing?

eve_ops: we rolled tokenizer v3.4.1 to canary last night and to prod at 03:12 UTC. The rollout included a different prompt-normalization step that changes prefix token boundaries.

mike.roy: that matches start time of spike (~03:20 UTC). hypothesis: tokenizer change altered prefix-key generation -> more collisions -> cache stampede + larger batches -> latency cliff.

sara.nguyen: customer-impact: several chat customers saw timeouts; CS reported 6 customers with degraded throughput. tagging @lia_support for list.

lia_support: got the list, contacting affected customers and offering rollback ETA. most are mid-market with high concurrency.

oncall_tier2: immediate mitigations proposed:
- throttle batch size at runtime to reduce tail latency (set max_batch_tokens=1024)
- enable prefix fallback to sha1-legacy hashing for critical routes
- invalidate prefix cache for suspect templates
- roll tokenizer back on canary (then prod) if needed

mike.roy: applying batch size throttle now via remote flag: `infractl set /runtime/batching/max_tokens 1024 --env prod`

sara.nguyen: executed. monitoring…

(1m later)

eve_ops: batch throttle applied. CPU pressure dropped on workers; p95 latency improving to ~350ms. kv miss rate still elevated though.

oncall_tier2: starting prefix cache sweep job to evict keys created since 03:10 UTC. command: ```
POST /admin/prefix-invalidate
{ "older_than": "2026-03-10T03:10:00Z", "prefixes": "auto-detect" }
```

mike.roy: launching fallback hasher for critical routes: `feature-flag:use_sha1_legacy=true` on rollout path. this will make prefix keys compatible with older tokenizer.

sara.nguyen: enabling safe-mode routing: route high-qps customers to dedicated pool with conservative batching and cache warming.

lia_support: update to all impacted customers: ETA for full mitigation ~ 25-40m. offering reroute and credits.

mike.roy: quick log excerpt showing the collision pattern:
```
2026-03-10T03:22:11Z worker-12 WARN kv-store miss for prefix_key=pf_0x7a2f (bucket 12)
2026-03-10T03:22:11Z worker-12 INFO batch_size=4096 tokens queued=4096 latency_ms=1280
2026-03-10T03:22:12Z worker-9 ERR serialize failed key_conflict pf_0x7a2f -> pf_0x7a2f
```

oncall_tier2: ok we have symptomatic relief from batching throttle and fallback. next: decide rollback vs targeted patch.

eve_ops: tokenizer rollback plan ready. canary revert -> monitor 10m -> prod revert in waves. rollback script: `deploy rollback tokenizer v3.4.0` (will require 3-min deploys per region).

mike.roy: prefer targeted hash compatibility shim that maps new tokens to legacy prefix space for ShortPrompt templates. less disruptive. patch PR open: `fix/prefix-hash-compat` (link: https://git.company/repo/pull/4821).

sara.nguyen: what about batching config persisted across restarts? ensure new default won't auto-upgrade.

eve_ops: setting cluster-defaults to conservative values and annotating in runbook. executed: `infractl set defaults.batch_tokens 1536`.

lia_support: updating customers with workaround steps and status updates. pings set for every 15m.

mike.roy: will merge compatibility shim if no regression in staging. rolling out to prod in 2 waves.

(20m later)

incident-bot: status update: p95 token latency back to ~220-400ms; error rates trending down; 4 customers still seeing intermittent timeouts.

lia_support: 3 customers accepted reroute; 1 requested immediate rollback.

sara.nguyen: agreed to rollback for that one if risk >1.5x SLA breach. coordinate with oncall and infra.

oncall_tier2: checklist for handoff to follow-up team (post-incident):
- finish PR review + deploy hash-compat shim
- run prefix-invalidate sweep verification and record keys evicted
- run full compatibility test matrix for tokenizer variations
- update runbook and add pre-deploy test for prefix-key drift
- postmortem with customer impact summary and timeline

mike.roy: I'll own the PR -> deploy. eve_ops take rollback runbook and infra defaults. sara.nguyen lead postmortem. lia_support own customer comms.

eve_ops: creating incident ticket in tracker: INC-2026-3142 and adding runbook links.

lia_support: will send follow-up note to impacted customers once final mitigation deployed.

sara.nguyen: thanks all — nice containment work. please keep logs and traces in the incident folder and tag me for postmortem kickoff.

mike.roy: tagging action items: `owner:mike.roy action:merge-shim due:2026-03-10T05:00:00Z`, `owner:eve_ops action:rollback-plan due:2026-03-10T04:30:00Z`, `owner:lia_support action:customer-comm due:2026-03-10T04:00:00Z`.

incident-bot: incident state -> mitigated. severity -> Sev2. handoff to followup triage.

sara.nguyen: starting postmortem draft. will include hypothesis, mitigations, and a pre-deploy tokenizer compatibility test to prevent prefix drift.

(END)
